Row.Text: When a settlement's people have a reason to rise, armed partisans appear in the countryside around it and fight under the game's own independent-power AI. A settlement won over by a rival's culture (Cultural Diffusion), a mistreated enclave (Emigration) or years of misery can start a rising; a National Park calms the countryside. Works alone or with those mods. Single-player and hotseat.

A settlement that joins a civilization by culture may rise against its new owner. The worse the two civilizations get on, the more likely it is; allies almost never, civilizations at war almost always.

With Emigration, a recognised enclave may take up arms against how it's treated: rarely while its host is at war with the community's homeland, much more often under one of Emigration's suspicion cards. A protective card lets the unrest settle.
Any settlement that stays at -10 Happiness or worse for twenty turns (at Standard speed) may rise, and the chance grows each turn it stays miserable.
Count culture flips from any mod
On: a settlement transferred by culture counts whichever mod did it. Off: only in games with Cultural Diffusion.
With National Parks, the Happiness a settlement's park tiles pay counts a second time against misery. Exploration and Modern Ages only.
Partisans gather here. Placed by the Partisans mod for one turn when a settlement's people first take up arms; it leaves as soon as the rebels have a hideout of their own.
